what_it_does: This paper describes a hidden data-theft channel that exploits the way cloud FPGAs (programmable chips rented in the cloud) communicate internally. The AXI protocol is a standard set of handshake signals — essentially digital "ready" and "valid" flags — that components inside an FPGA use to pass data to each other. By deliberately delaying or hastening those handshake signals, an attacker can encode secret information into the timing gaps between network packets leaving the machine. A receiver outside the cloud can then decode those timing patterns and reconstruct the stolen data. The key novelty is that this channel produces very little unusual network traffic, making it hard for cloud providers to detect.
